newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sees reasonable vine harvest despite weather.
newsitem.headline: Italy sees reasonable vine harvest despite weather.

text.p: The growth process at vineyards in all Italian production areas is progressing normally, the Italian Institute for Agriculture Studies (Ismea) said.
Moreover, Ismea said in a statement, the prolonged lack of rainfall has reduced negative phytosanitary consequences to a minimum, allowing the crop cycle to continue satisfactorily.

According to preliminary estimates of the 1997 grape harvest, although a decline is expected in Friuli following an exceptional year, an abundant harvest is forecast in the Cuneo area, especially for Dolcetto and Barbera grapes.

Producers in the Oltrepo Pavese zone were also positive, apart from some doubts over Pinot, while in the Veneto region white grapes were developing normally but red grapes were likely to show a fall in production.
As for the central Italian area, first estimates for the Lazio region indicated a slight decline in harvests due to the April frosts, with some damage to early grape varieties.
